beats.say: The Orionids meteor shower occurs annually and lasts approximately one week in late October.
The first detail is that these meteors normally peak around 21 to 22 October.
Secondly, in some years you can see 50 to 70 meteors per hour.
This annual event is actually caused by debris from Halley's Comet.
The third detail is its 75 to 76 year orbit, last passing in 1986.

facts: The Orionids meteor shower occurs annually and lasts approximately one week in late October
In some years meteors may occur at rates of 50 to 70 per hour
The Orionids normally peak around 21 to 22 October
Halley's Comet was named after astronomer Edmund Halley
Halley's Comet last passed through the inner Solar System in 1986 on its 75 to 76 year orbit
